public_rationale: The age assertion is contradicted: a March 23, 2011 report described i/o New Jersey's planned capacity of up to 100 MW, documenting the concept about fifteen years before the claim [e1]. The other components remain unresolved: Epoch AI's November 10, 2025 forecast of gigawatt-scale facilities coming online in early 2026 does not verify their operating status on March 24, 2026 or disprove Zitron's reported unsuccessful search [e2]. OpenAI announced $110 billion in new investment on February 27, 2026 [e3]. The Decoder reported on February 21, 2026 that OpenAI ended 2025 with roughly $40 billion in cash and cash equivalents [e4]. Neither item matches available March liquidity against obligations due, so neither settles the assertion about paying bills [e3] [e4].
limitations: The contradiction concerns the age of the 100 MW concept; the 2011 report does not establish that all 100 MW was operating.
The packet lacks comprehensive commissioning records for gigawatt campuses as of March 24, 2026.
Announced investment does not establish cash received, and the year-end cash figure comes from secondary reporting.
No matched liquidity, obligations-due and payment records establish OpenAI's payment capacity on the publication date.

our_interpretation: This combines three assertions requiring different evidence. They are retained together because only one claim_id was supplied.
The age assertion concerns the history of the 100 MW concept before publication. The target period therefore has no specified historical starting date.

For the operating-capacity assertion, the ordinary reading is a single campus with approximately 1 GW commissioned and usable by March 24, 2026. Announced ultimate capacity and aggregate capacity across unrelated sites do not qualify.
The wording reports the author's unsuccessful search. It is weaker than an unqualified assertion that no such facility exists.

For OpenAI, the ordinary reading is inability to meet obligations when due, rather than operating losses or dependence on investors. The latest year-end cash position reported before the post is relevant financial context, but cannot alone establish March payment capacity.
No accounting basis is supplied for the assertion about paying bills.
criteria.support_condition: Historical records establish that the 100 MW concept emerged only a few years before publication; sufficiently comprehensive operating records establish the apparent absence of a commissioned 1 GW campus; and contemporaneous liquidity and payment records show OpenAI could not meet bills due.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A substantially older documented 100 MW design contradicts the age component. A verified operating 1 GW campus by publication contradicts the implied absence component. Matched liquidity and obligations records demonstrating payment capacity contradict the OpenAI component. Findings must identify which component they settle.

This was a forecast, not a commissioning record. It identifies plausible candidates but cannot establish their actual status on March 24.
